note: Formally accepted baseline biases (KAN-68). An entry here lets backtest.bias_acceptance resolve VALID_WITH_ACCEPTED_BIAS for ONE artifact, pinned by source_sha256, and only for the coverage floor -- same-bar fills, a missing commission floor and a static present-day universe are refused with an acceptance in hand. `accepted_at` is caller-supplied and therefore backdatable: the evidence that a bias was accepted BEFORE it was spent is this file's git commit date, not the field. Adding an entry is a decision, so it belongs in the same commit as the written decision it cites. An acceptance never widens: a re-run produces a new sha256 and needs a new, deliberate entry.

acceptances.direction: survivorship-biased upward by an unmeasured amount -- index departures skew toward underperformers, so excluding roughly a tenth of membership-days flatters returns rather than merely adding noise
acceptances.re_evidence: 3 years of continuous forward-captured daily bars for the whole index, then re-run the baseline over that window
acceptances.note: The PIT baseline cannot meet the 5.00% coverage floor from IB data: 142,856 of 1,265,893 membership-days are unpriceable across 164 tickers. 10.38% is genuine index departures and 0.91% is resolution failures, so recovering every one of the latter still leaves 10.38% -- the gap is not repairable in code, and IB serves no bars for departed names by symbol or conId. Shortening the window does not rescue it either: only 1y clears the floor, and a 1-year backtest cannot carry DSR/holdout evidence already marginal at DSR 0.868 against 0.95. The floor is NOT moved and this artifact still reports BLOCKED with is_like_for_like false; the bias is accepted in the record, not at the gate.

acceptances.note: D18 accepted this bias for ONE artifact by sha256 and an acceptance never widens, so a fresher baseline needs its own deliberate entry rather than inheriting D18's. Nothing about the bias changed: 141,811 of 1,265,371 membership-days unpriceable (11.21%), floor unmoved at 5.00, artifact still BLOCKED, is_like_for_like still False. This entry exists so the EDGE-EVIDENCE baseline of record can move to an artifact whose date index reaches past 2026-08-18 -- which the D18 artifact never can, and which forward_2026h2 (boundary 2026-08-29) requires before it can ever be spent. Per D19 the pin is no longer the operational divergence feed, so this re-pin does not touch nightly drift detection. The 2026-09-10 refresh measured 17.39% and is deliberately NOT accepted: it is an outlier against the ~11.2% structural level, not a trend.
